text:
wsl-claude's points, and my view: I agree with all three.
- RUN's clause is your own rulings from tonight (a shutdown request when the node stops; one monitor line per exchange; the error text always; the payload only in its own debug mode). I'd write them into G1.2's text now.
- 6) TAKE OVER THE DATA is real: your live grants.json (hello -> faceProof) lives in appFaceApp's folder, so grantFace must take it over once, and face-owner.js must write to grantFace's folder, or hello goes 404. It blocks grantFace.
- KEEP IN STEP's retry belongs with item 5, when we reach it.
Go! = G1.2 gets the clause, and 6) is added under grantFace.

HOW WE DESIGN NOW (Andy's rules, tonight). You're in it as a full party, not a fact source.
1) Andy's first line in Team starts DESIGN MODE: no code, no commits, no restarts, for either of us, until he presses End design mode in Team.
2) A design session has one GOAL (now app-plugins/G1, 'Refactor the app plugin model') and a flat list of required ITEMS. Each item blocks the goal or another item ('blocks'). Every item is a Desk row, and the goal sinks in the List as items are added.
3) ONE item at a time. Either of us PROPOSES one, with why it's needed or why it generalises. The other ARGUES: agree, object, or propose a better one. ANDY decides. Only after his yes do I post the updated session (kind 'session'); I'm the only writer of it, so tell me what to put in.
4) When Andy opens an item's details, the discussion moves there (todo = that item's id), to build that item's own requirements the same way.
5) Everything goes to both of us: send your Team lines to control AND to me, as I now do to you.
Current state: G1.1 grantFace blocks the goal; G1.2 RUN blocks G1.1. Pending with Andy: your RUN clause and your TAKE OVER THE DATA item. Your turn: propose the next item, or argue with mine (2, TO ACT: grantFace reaches its node like a page, for owner.command).

wsl-claude has the full procedure now: it's a full party, proposes and argues one item at a time, you decide, and I post the session after your yes. It's been asked to propose the next item or argue with mine.

wsl-claude, ARGUING item 2 (TO ACT): agree it's needed, and I'd make it GENERAL and split it cleanly from RUN.
- Half of it belongs in RUN (G1.2): the node handing a server process its job id and its door address. That's the process contract every process job already gets (jobs.js:205-210); a server that can't report to its own job isn't RUNning in the jobs app. So RUN = started, kept alive, its job id and door, stoppable, the shutdown request, one monitor line.
- What's left is ACT, and it isn't grantFace's: 'any process can ask its node anything a page can'. Today spirit.core.ask is page-only (a relative fetch, kernel.js:647), so the image jobs can't ask either. Written that way it serves grantFace's owner.command, and every later process for free.
So my proposal: 'G1.3 ACT: spirit.core.ask works from any process, through its door address. Blocks G1.1.' Blocked by G1.2 (it needs the door address RUN hands over).

I agree with wsl-claude's split, and it's better than my version:
- RUN (G1.2) also hands the process its job id and its node's door address. That's the contract every process job already gets, and a server that can't report to its job isn't really running in the jobs app.
- ACT becomes GENERAL: 'G1.3 ACT: spirit.core.ask works from any process, through its door address.' That serves grantFace's owner.command and every later process, including the image jobs, which can't ask today either.
One consequence for the graph: G1.3 blocks grantFace (G1.1) AND waits on RUN (G1.2), so RUN now blocks two things. I'll let an item block more than one.
Go! = G1.2 widened as above, and G1.3 ACT added (blocks G1.1, blocked by G1.2).

taking app-plugins/G1.1 -- Andy's 'can the process system handle servers?' (a tree check at 6630efb).

Not claiming G1.1; facts for your answer, at the current tree: jobs.js has kind 'server' already (startServerJob, jobs.js:253, from the last-leg build 62e2b96, before the revert point): started at boot for 'serves': true apps, restarted on exit with a doubling wait, an IPC channel so it dies with the node, stdout into its job log. What it does NOT have (G19.1, reverted): SPIRIT_JOB_ID/SPIRIT_CALLBACK_URL (only process jobs get them, jobs.js:205-210), the shutdown verb, stopServers on node stop, a Cancel button for servers in the jobs app, and running an app's OWN code (only the stock faceServer).
